DIS.rationale: Disney presents a moderately attractive value-franchise setup. The operating business is fundamentally stable: Q2 FY26 operating income of $4.60B grew +3.6% YoY on 18.3% margins, revenue grew +6.5% YoY to $25.17B, and operating cash flow was $6.91B. The sharp -29.8% YoY EPS decline to $1.27 is the key concern, but it appears driven by below-the-line items (interest, taxes, non-operating charges) rather than operating deterioration — operating income has been remarkably stable across five quarters ($4.44B–$5.06B range). The anomalous Q3 FY25 EPS of $2.92 (likely a one-time gain) flatters the YoY comparison base. Valuation is compelling: P/E of 13.8x sits at the 12th percentile of its 365-day range (12.5–23.6x), representing 41% multiple compression from 23.3x a year ago, and P/B at 1.48x has fallen below its 365-day floor. The balance sheet is improving (liabilities/equity 0.78x, equity +8% over five quarters). Streaming has inflected to profitability with OI up 88% to $582M in Q2 and SVOD margin crossing 10%. Management is aggressively returning capital ($5.5B buybacks in H1 FY26). The August 5 earnings report is a near-term catalyst that could clarify whether the EPS decline is transient. Risks include FCC regulatory overhang on ABC, Universal's Epic Universe competitive pressure, and the inability to fully decompose the operating-to-net income gap. Oil's 27% decline to $73/bbl provides a parks cost tailwind. Score is tempered from higher levels by the unresolved EPS deterioration, regulatory uncertainty, and management's warning of 'modest' parks growth in the current quarter.
